title: Basic 6 · Mirror an image (MR)
summary: Flip an image across its horizontal or vertical centre line — SPIDER's MR command. Useful for handedness tests.

steps.title: Try mirroring
steps.body: Flip an image across an axis. For cryo-EM particles this is used to detect/fix handedness (mirror-image), to grow a reference set under an assumed symmetry, or to re-orient particles after a CTF phase flip. SPIDER's `MR`.

steps.title: Drop the data node
steps.body: From Palette (Data), drag **Test · Clock face**. The clock is asymmetric both horizontally and vertically, so the effect of a mirror is immediately visible.

steps.title: Run the graph to check
steps.body: Press ▶ Run graph so `data.clock` shows its image before we attach the flip.

steps.title: Wire Clock → Flip
steps.body: Drag from Clock's `image` output to Flip's `image` input.

steps.title: Run the graph to check
steps.body: Press ▶ Run graph. With the default axis you'll see one mirror direction already — a baseline before we flip the other way.

steps.title: Click Flip
steps.body: Click Flip. The Inspector's `axis` dropdown selects `horizontal` (left-right flip = mirror about the x axis) or `vertical` (top-bottom = mirror about the y axis).

steps.title: Set axis to vertical
steps.body: Change `axis` to **`vertical`**. Top-bottom mirror — the 12 moves down, the 6 moves up, and both digits themselves appear upside down (mirrored glyphs).

steps.title: Run the graph
steps.body: Press ▶ Run graph. The Flip node preview shows the clock face mirrored top-to-bottom.

steps.title: 🎉 Done
steps.body: Switch `axis` to `horizontal` for a left-right flip: 12 and 6 stay in place but their glyphs mirror; 3 and 9 swap positions (both appearing as mirror characters). Important: a mirror only **flips pixel positions** — the glyph itself is also reflected (an "E" becomes "Ǝ"), not re-read as a different digit. Mirror is a linear map, so combining it with rotation (Basic 1) lets you build pairs of references that differ only by a single handedness flip — useful for growing the reference set during mirror-aware alignment.
